s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with palpitations and transient loss of consciousness
salient_findings: Syncope with preceding palpitation and amaurosis
Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during presyncope episode
Diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and mid-right coronary artery
key_facts: 50-year-old male patient
Experienced syncope 30 minutes before admission
Reported palpitation and amaurosis before loss of consciousness
Previous episode of syncope 1 month prior
Diabetes, well controlled with medication
Vital signs: blood pressure 125/96 mm Hg, pulse rate 81 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 99% under ambient air
Normal physical examination results
Normal laboratory tests, including blood glucose, electrolytes, D-dimer, troponin I, and N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide
Normal electrocardiogram and transthoracic echocardiography
Abnormal 12-lead 24-hour Holter monitoring with polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and QTc of 403 milliseconds
Coronary Angiography showed 50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and 80% stenosis in mid-right coronary artery

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: QTc of 403 milliseconds and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during presyncope episode

shortlist.label: Coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: 50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and 80% stenosis in mid-right coronary artery

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and recurrent syncope

shortlist.label: Brugada syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ST-segment elevation in leads I, aVL, and V1 to V5

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of palpitation and amaurosis before loss of consciousness, along with the Holter monitoring results showing polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, are consistent with catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. The normal electrocardiogram and echocardiography results also support this diagnosis, as CPVT often has a normal cardiac structure.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The QTc interval of 403 milliseconds is within the normal range for most adults, making Long QT syndrome less likely.

rejected.label: Coronary artery disease
rejected.why: While the patient has significant coronary artery stenosis, the symptoms and Holter monitoring results suggest an arrhythmic cause of syncope rather than a cardiac ischemic event.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no evidence of right ventricular dysfunction or structural abnormalities on echocardiography to support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Brugada syndrome
rejected.why: The electrocardiogram did not show the characteristic ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V3 that is typical of Brugada syndrome.
